pageCache.pageTitle: All Saints Catholic College | Catholic Secondary School in London
pageCache.text:
A Catholic school shaped by faith and community
Helping every student grow into who they are called to be
A school where every
﻿student is known
All Saints Catholic College is a Catholic secondary school in North Kensington where students are known, challenged and supported.
We combine high expectations with strong pastoral care, helping students grow in faith, character and learning.
Faith and formation
Our Catholic ethos shapes the way we learn, care for one another and build community.
Learning and ambition
Students are encouraged to work hard, develop confidence and prepare well for life beyond school.
A broad and ambitious curriculum
Students at All Saints Catholic College follow a broad and balanced curriculum designed to build knowledge, confidence and curiosity.
From Key Stage 3 through to GCSE options, we help students develop strong foundations, discover their strengths and prepare well for further study, work and adult life.
Curriculum overview
Understand the structure, purpose and ambition of learning across the school.
Subjects
Explore the subjects taught at All Saints Catholic College, including GCSE pathways.
Faith at the heart
of school life
As a Catholic school, All Saints Catholic College seeks to help students grow as people of faith, hope and service.
Our motto, Orare. Laborare. Servire. means to pray, to work, to serve. It shapes the way we learn, care for one another and contribute to the wider community.
Prayer and Worship
Students are invited to grow in faith through prayer, reflection, liturgy and the rhythm of the Catholic year.
Service and community
Faith is lived through care for others, strong relationships and a commitment to the common good.
Schola
﻿Cantorum
Our student choir supports worship and school celebrations, helping students grow in musical skill, confidence and service.
Exceptional Results﻿
Our latest inspection outcomes highlight the strength of our provision across the school. We are incredibly proud to have received three Exceptional judgements and three Strong Standard judgements.
These results demonstrate our unwavering focus on excellence, wellbeing, and continuous improvement for every young person in our community.

pageCache.pageTitle: Catholic Life | All Saints Catholic College
pageCache.text:
Faith lived daily
Faith shapes daily life at All Saints through prayer, reflection, and service to others.
Faith at the heart
﻿of school life
The Catholic ethos is at the heart of our school community.Faith is not separate from school life; it shapes how we learn, relate, and grow together.
Daily reflection
Each school day includes time for prayer and reflection.
These take place in assemblies, tutor time, and Religious Education lessons, led by both students and staff.
Whole school Masses and liturgies follow the seasons of the Church, giving the community regular opportunities to gather in prayer.
Parish and
﻿sacramental life
We value our links with local parishes and support students in celebrating the sacraments.
Students are given opportunities to participate in Mass, reconciliation, and other aspects of parish life.
House Saints
At All Saints Catholic College, each of our Houses is inspired by a saint whose life shows us how to live our faith.
Simon of Cyrene teaches us to help those who are struggling, and Anne shows us the value of family and faith. Ignatius of Loyola invites us to find God in all things, while Nicholas Owen gives an example of quiet courage and loyalty. Teresa of Ávila and Catherine of Siena, both Doctors of the Church, remind us of the strength that comes from prayer and from speaking up for what is right.
Together, our House Saints inspire students to serve others, be brave and grow in faith.
Retreat experiences
Each year group takes part in an annual retreat, designed to support spiritual reflection and personal growth.
These experiences provide time away from the routine of school life to reflect, build relationships, and grow in faith.
Dei Verbum
and Lectio Divina
“I have come so that you may have life; life in all its fullness.” (John 10:10)
Dei Verbum, meaning Word of God, is a weekly Gospel reflection used across the school.
Students are invited to reflect on the Gospel and consider how its message connects to everyday life, both in school and beyond.
“Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path.”
Lectio Divina, meaning Divine Reading, is a more reflective way of engaging with Scripture.
Students are guided to listen, reflect, and consider how the Gospel speaks into their own lives.
These reflections take place during tutor time and form part of the rhythm of school life.
Living the gospel
Students are encouraged to live out Gospel values through acts of service and outreach.
Care for others is part of daily life at All Saints.
Supporting charities such as CAFOD
Community outreach initiatives
School prayer
Help us today and always, to strengthen our faith in you.
Guide us in our work, to enable us to become more like you.
Encourage us to follow the example of the Saints,
to live our lives in service to others,
and to bring about your Kingdom here on earth.

pageCache.pageTitle: Faith in Action | All Saints Catholic College
pageCache.text:
Faith in action
Living our Catholic faith through service, generosity and care for others.
Putting faith
﻿into action
At All Saints Catholic College, faith is not only something we speak about. It is something we try to live.
Our Catholic mission calls us to notice the needs of others, respond generously and build a community where every person is valued. Through fundraising, charitable work and acts of service, students are encouraged to see that even small actions can make a real difference.
Our work is shaped by three key pillars: Educatio, providing excellent learning; Formatio, nurturing faith and character; and Iustitia Socialis, fostering a commitment to justice and service to others, both locally and globally.
Supporting charities throughout the year
Throughout the school year, students and staff raise money for a range of charities and good causes. We work with and support organisations including Mary’s Meals, Macmillan Cancer Support, Catholic Children’s Society, Women’s Aid and other charities chosen by the school community.
Fundraising at All Saints is often full of energy and imagination. Students find their own ways to get involved, from sponsored walks and collections to themed events and form-group challenges. It is a practical way for young people to learn generosity, compassion and responsibility.
Community
﻿Christmas dinner
One of the most loved examples of Faith in Action at All Saints is the Community Christmas Dinner.
Each December, the school welcomes older members of the local community for a proper Christmas dinner, bringing people together for food, conversation, warmth and celebration. It is a simple but powerful act of hospitality, and a reminder that Catholic education is about serving the wider community, not only those within the school gates.
Students and staff help make the event special by creating a welcoming atmosphere and sharing the joy of Christmas with local residents.
Christmas
﻿shoebox appeal
The school also supports seasonal acts of giving, including the Christmas Shoebox Appeal. These projects give students and families a practical way to share kindness and support people who may be facing difficulty at Christmas.
Further details are shared with families when these appeals take place.

The Mission Fund
Supporting the students, facilities and wider mission of All Saints Catholic College.
Supporting the life
﻿of the school
We are grateful for the generosity of our school community in supporting All Saints Catholic College.
Contributions to The Mission Fund help enhance the educational experience of our students, supporting the school environment, future-facing learning and opportunities that help young people grow in confidence, spirituality, wellbeing and academic success.
Make a regular
or one-off gift
Through the Parents’ Regular Giving Scheme, known as The Mission Fund, families are invited to consider making a regular donation or a one-off gift to the School Fund.
Giving is entirely voluntary. We understand that family circumstances vary, and every decision is treated with respect and confidentiality.
£10 per month
£20 per month
£30 per month
£50 single donation
Increase the value
﻿of your gift
If you are a UK taxpayer, Gift Aid may allow the school to claim additional money on your donation at no extra cost to you.
Please complete the Gift Aid form when making a donation.
Gift Aid Form →
Could your employer match your gift
Some employers support charitable giving through matched giving schemes. This means they may match donations made by employees to registered charities, sometimes doubling the value of a gift at no extra cost to the donor.
All Saints Catholic College has provided a list of companies understood to offer matched giving. This list is intended as a helpful guide only, as schemes can change and eligibility may vary.
Please check directly with your employer’s Payroll, HR or Corporate Social Responsibility team to confirm whether matched giving is available and how to apply.
How your support helps
The Mission Fund helps sustain and develop the school, supporting facilities and opportunities that benefit students now and in the future.
Learning opportunities
Supporting resources and opportunities that enrich students’ education.
Facilities & environment
Helping maintain and enhance spaces for learning, formation and community.
Whole-person formation
Supporting the school’s commitment to academic excellence, confidence, spirituality and wellbeing.
Regular giving & matched giving enquiries
For questions about regular giving, Gift Aid or matched giving, please contact the school office.

pageCache.pageTitle: About All Saints Catholic College | Catholic Secondary School
pageCache.text:
A Catholic school where faith shapes learning and community
A community where every student is known, supported, and encouraged to grow in faith, character, and purpose.
A Catholic community of faith, learning and care
All Saints Catholic College is a Catholic secondary school where faith shapes learning, relationships and daily life.
We want every student to be known, challenged and supported, growing not only in knowledge, but in character, confidence and purpose.
Faith and Formation
Academic Excellence
Strong Community
Life at All Saints
School life at All Saints is shaped by strong relationships, high expectations and a deep commitment to the dignity of every young person.
Students are encouraged to take full part in the life of the school, to develop their gifts, and to contribute generously to the community around them.
Every student is known and valued
Faith is lived daily
Strong relationships shape school life
Our Mission and Ethos
Orare. Laborare. Servire.
To pray, to work, to serve.﻿
This is more than a motto. It shapes daily life at All Saints Catholic College.
Rooted in the Catholic faith, we seek to form young people who are thoughtful, resilient and generous. We want students to grow in wisdom, work with purpose and learn to serve others with courage and compassion.
Mr Walton﻿
It is my privilege to welcome you to All Saints Catholic College.
Our vision is rooted in the Gospel: “I have come so that you may have life; life in all its fullness” (John 10:10). Guided by this Gospel truth, we are committed to helping every student flourish academically, spiritually and personally. Christ is at the heart of all that we do, inspiring our mission to provide an outstanding education grounded in Gospel values and the rich tradition of the Catholic faith.
Through our motto — Orare, Laborare, Servire (Pray, Work, Serve) — we seek to form young people who think deeply, act justly and serve generously. We believe education is about much more than academic success; it is about developing the whole person and enabling each student to discover and fulfil their God-given potential.
We are proud to be a high-achieving school where students make excellent progress and achieve strong outcomes. We hold high expectations for every learner and are committed to ensuring that all young people leave us well prepared for the next stage of education, employment and life.
A fulfilling education, however, extends far beyond the classroom. Students at All Saints benefit from a rich programme of enrichment opportunities in sport, music, the creative arts, faith, leadership and service. These experiences broaden horizons, build character and develop confidence, helping our students to live life in all its fullness.
Our work is shaped by three key pillars: Educatio, providing excellent learning; Formatio, nurturing faith and character; and Iustitia Socialis, fostering a commitment to justice and service to others, both locally and globally.
The strength of our community lies in the dedication of our staff, governors and leaders, who work together to model Christ’s love through service, integrity and compassion. As a Christ-centred community, we walk together in faith, recognising Christ in one another and encouraging every student to lead with hope, courage and purpose.
We hope this website gives you a glimpse into the vibrant life of our school and all that makes All Saints such a special place to learn, grow and flourish.

Friends of ASCC Performing Arts
Supporting music, drama and performance opportunities for students at All Saints Catholic College.
Opening doors through music and performance
At All Saints Catholic College, the Performing Arts play an important part in the life and mission of the school.
Learning an instrument, singing in an ensemble or performing in a school production helps students grow in confidence, discipline, creativity and friendship. It gives young people opportunities to express themselves, work with others and discover gifts that may stay with them for life.
Making opportunity available to every student
All Saints is committed to ensuring that every child can access life-changing opportunities in music and performance, whatever their background.
With over 40% of students on Free School Meals and over 50% speaking English as an additional language, the school works hard to remove financial barriers and make Performing Arts provision available to as many students as possible.
Performing Arts
﻿in Numbers
The school already provides a rich and ambitious Performing Arts offer.
200+ music lessons each week
Students take part in more than 200 music lessons a week across the school.
15 instruments
Students can access tuition across 15 different instruments, supported by specialist tutors.
107 students in the
﻿school musical
This year, 107 students took part in the school musical, with a further 25 students working backstage.
How your support helps
Donations to Friends of ASCC Performing Arts directly support opportunities for students who may not otherwise be able to access them.

﻿tuition
Helping subsidise lessons and specialist teaching.
Instruments loans
Supporting students who need access to instruments.
Ensemble coaching
Providing opportunities to rehearse, perform and grow as musicians.

﻿costs
Helping remove financial barriers to graded music examinations.

Supporting school musicals, performances, scenery, backstage work and technical opportunities.

To sustain and grow this vital work, we invite families, friends and supporters to make a one-off donation to Friends of ASCC Performing Arts.

Preparing students
﻿for life beyond school
A structured careers programme that builds ambition, confidence, and real-world understanding
Careers at All Saints
Our careers programme helps students take meaningful steps towards their future, building ambition, confidence and the ability to make informed choices about education and employment.
Through PSHE lessons, tutor time, visiting speakers, and links with the local community, students develop the skills and awareness needed to succeed beyond school.
How students
﻿are supported
Students receive structured support at each stage, helping them understand opportunities, build confidence, and prepare for life beyond school.﻿
Key Stage 3 (Years 7-9)
Students begin exploring different career pathways, developing awareness of opportunities and understanding their strengths and interests.
Key Stage 4 (Years 10-11)
Students receive more targeted support, including meetings with employers and further education providers, as well as preparation for post-16 pathways.﻿
Work experience
All students complete a one-week work experience placement in Year 10, helping them develop confidence and real-world skills.
Our careers programme
Our careers programme is guided by the Gatsby Benchmarks and the Career Development Institute framework, ensuring students receive high-quality, structured careers education.
A stable careers programme

All students are given opportunities to meet with apprenticeship and technical education providers in line with national guidance.
These experiences help students understand a wide range of pathways, including apprenticeships, T Levels and further education.

Relationships and
﻿Sex Education
How Relationships and Sex Education is taught at All Saints Catholic College.
Relationships
﻿and sex education
Relationships and Sex Education (RSE) is a statutory part of the school curriculum.
At All Saints Catholic College, it is taught in a way that reflects both statutory guidance and the school's Catholic ethos.
Our programme﻿
We use the Life to the Full programme, developed by Ten Ten Resources, to support the delivery of RSE.
The programme meets statutory requirements while reflecting the Catholic understanding of the human person, relationships, and dignity.
Students are supported in developing knowledge, understanding, and maturity in ways appropriate to their age and stage of development.
What is taught
Students follow a structured RSE programme across each year group, building understanding over time.
Who am I?
Healthy inside and out
Where we come from
Friends and family
My life on screen
Living in the wider world
Created not chosen
Appreciating differences
Before I was born
Tough relationships
Think before you share
The wider world
Searching for love
Objectification
In control of your choices
Fertility and contraception
Marriage
Knowing your rights and responsibilities
Authentic freedom
Self-image
Values, attitudes and beliefs
Parenthood
Pregnancy and abortion
Solidarity﻿
Self-worth
Addiction
Eating disorders
Fertility
Pornography
Coercive control
A Catholic approach
RSE at All Saints Catholic College is rooted in the belief that every person is created with dignity and purpose.
Students are encouraged to reflect on relationships, choices, and responsibility in light of the Gospel and the Church's teaching.
This approach ensures that learning is both informative and formative.
Information for parents
Parents are encouraged to engage with the RSE programme and can request further information about the content delivered at each stage.
If you have any questions, please contact the school.

pageCache.pageTitle: Curriculum Overview | All Saints Catholic College
pageCache.text:
What students learn
A broad and balanced curriculum that builds knowledge, confidence and prepares students for life beyond school.
Our curriculum
At All Saints Catholic College, our curriculum is designed to develop knowledge, understanding and confidence across a broad range of subjects.
Students follow a structured programme of study that supports academic progress while encouraging curiosity, independence and personal growth.
Learning is carefully sequenced from Year 7 through to GCSE, ensuring students build strong foundations and are well prepared for the next stage of their education.
A Catholic approach to education
At All Saints Catholic College, education is grounded in the belief that every student is called to grow and flourish.
Inspired by the Gospel, we aim to develop the whole person, supporting students academically, spiritually, and personally so they are prepared for life beyond school.
Our curriculum reflects this vision, encouraging students to pursue knowledge, act with integrity, and develop a lifelong love of learning.
Our work is shaped by three key pillars: Educatio, providing excellent learning; Formatio, nurturing faith and character; and Iustitia Socialis, fostering a commitment to justice and service to others, both locally and globally.
Key stages﻿
Students follow a structured curriculum across Key Stage 3 and Key Stage 4, building knowledge and skills over time
Years 7-9﻿
Students study a broad range of subjects, developing core knowledge, skills and confidence.
Learning is designed to build strong foundations and prepare students for GCSE study.
Years 10-11﻿
﻿Students continue core subjects alongside GCSE options, following a pathway that reflects their strengths and future goals.
Learning becomes more specialised, preparing students for further education and future pathways.
How students learn
Teaching at All Saints Catholic College aims to challenge, support, and inspire every student.
Lessons are carefully designed to develop understanding gradually, with clear explanations, regular feedback, and opportunities for students to think independently and apply their knowledge.
Teachers set high expectations while offering the guidance and encouragement students need to succeed, making sure every learner is supported to make strong progress.

ASCC Dance Sirens
Our All Saints Sirens are back!
Our Dance Energy 2026 winners are having a fantastic start to the year, with the Sirens Dance Team going from strength to strength.
This year, our pupils are having the brilliant opportunity to be taught by a professional dancer from the Royal Academy of Dance, developing their skills in street and contemporary dance.
It is wonderful to see pupils growing in confidence, learning new techniques, working together and, most importantly, enjoying being part of the team.
We are so proud of our Sirens and can’t wait to see what they achieve this year!

Free school meals
Information about eligibility, how to apply, and support available for families.
Free school meals
Free school meals are available to support families and ensure all students have access to a nutritious meal during the school day.
If your child is eligible, this also allows the school to receive additional funding to support their education.
From September 2026, all children in households receiving Universal Credit can receive free school meals, regardless of household income.
We strongly encourage all families who have not applied yet, to apply for free school meals as the rules surrounding free school meals are changing. Even if your child already receives free meals, you must reapply before the Autumn term under the new rules. The school will then be able to recheck your eligibility each year which is a new requirement.
Please visit Free school meals | Royal Borough of Kensington and Chelsea to complete the application form.
Who can apply
You may be eligible for free school meals if you receive certain government benefits.
If you are unsure, we recommend checking directly with the local authority.
Universal Credit (subject to income threshold)
Income Support
Income-based Jobseeker’s Allowance
Income-related Employment and Support Allowance
The guarantee element of State Pension Credit
How to apply
To apply for free school meals, please contact the school office:
The school will guide you through the application process.
Why it matters
Even if your child does not take a free school meal, registering eligibility allows the school to receive additional funding.
This funding, known as Pupil Premium, helps provide additional support, resources, and opportunities for students.
Further benefits
Families who are registered for free school meals may also be eligible for additional support, including:
Holiday activity programmes with meals provided
Access to additional school support and resources
Catering and
﻿lunch information
All Saints Catholic College works with Accent Catering to provide breakfast, breaktime snacks and lunch for students.
Breakfast is available free of charge to all students from 7.45 am each morning. Students can also purchase food at breaktime and lunchtime.
For menus, dietary requirements and catering information, please visit the School Catering page.

pageCache.text:
History of the school
The story of All Saints Catholic College, its Catholic roots and its continuing mission in North Kensington.
A school shaped by faith and community
All Saints Catholic College is a relatively new school with a much deeper story behind it.
The buildings and community that now form All Saints have been shaped by generations of Catholic education in North Kensington. Across different names, structures and seasons of change, the purpose has remained constant: to serve young people and families through faith, learning and community.
From foundation to today
Redevelopment after the Blitz
After the Second World War, the buildings now associated with All Saints had been badly damaged during the Blitz. In 1946, the Archdiocese of Westminster took over the buildings for redevelopment.
St Charles Primary opens
St Charles Primary opened on the site, serving families in the local Catholic community.
Cardinal Manning schools open
Cardinal Manning Boys School opened in 1955, followed by Cardinal Manning Girls School in 1958.
Sion-Manning Catholic Girls’ School
During the 1960s, Cardinal Manning Girls merged with a convent school founded by the Sisters of Sion at Chepstow Villas, Bayswater. This formed Sion-Manning Catholic Girls’ School.
All Saints Catholic College
In September 2018, the school became All Saints Catholic College, a co-educational 11–16 school, admitting boys for the first time. that admitted
Honouring the past, serving the future
All Saints Catholic College holds its history close while continuing to build a school for today's students and families.
The legacy of St Charles, Cardinal Manning and Sion-Manning remains part of the school’s identity. That history continues through the students, staff, families and wider community who shape All Saints Catholic College today.
The Manning Award for excellence
In 2018, the school launched The Manning Award for Excellence in honour of its rich history.
The award is a year-long programme designed to challenge students and help them develop skills for sixth form, university and life beyond school. Students complete a dissertation-style project on a subject of their choosing, carrying out research and exploring a question linked to their chosen topic.
Through the Manning Award, students are encouraged to think deeply, work independently and grow in confidence as learners.
Continuing the story
The story of All Saints Catholic College is still being written.
Rooted in Catholic education and shaped by the local community, the school continues to look forward while remembering the people, places and traditions that helped form it.
